name: Training Data Store
description: Collects and persists training examples (input + remote response pairs) per task type. Stores as JSON-lines files in a configurable directory. Tracks example count per task. Automatically holds out a configurable percentage (default 10%) as a validation/test set (deterministic split based on SHA-256 hash of input for reproducibility). Signals when batch size threshold (fine_tune_batch_size) is reached for a task, triggering fine-tuning. Supports appending new examples without rewriting existing data. Provides iterators for training set and validation set separately. Designed as a typing.Protocol with a concrete filesystem-backed implementation. Storage layout: one JSONL file per task type at {base_dir}/{task_type}.jsonl, plus {base_dir}/_counts.json for fast count lookups reconciled on startup.

types.name: TrainingExample

fields.name: input
fields.description: The original input text sent to the remote model.

validators.error_message: Input must be a non-empty string.

fields.name: output
fields.description: The response text received from the remote model.

validators.error_message: Output must be a non-empty string.

fields.name: task_type
fields.description: The task type identifier that this example belongs to. Used to partition storage into per-task JSONL files. Must be a valid filesystem-safe string.

validators.error_message: task_type must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores.
task_type must be between 1 and 128 characters.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: ISO 8601 datetime string indicating when this example was captured. Serialized as string for JSONL compatibility; parsed as datetime internally.

validators.error_message: Timestamp must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z).

fields.name: metadata
fields.description: Optional metadata dictionary for additional context (e.g., model name, latency, token count). All values must be JSON-serializable.

types.description: A single training example record representing an input/output pair captured from a remote API response, persisted as one line in a JSONL file.

types.name: TrainingDataStoreConfig

fields.name: base_dir
fields.description: Filesystem path to the directory where JSONL files and _counts.json are stored. Will be auto-created (including parents) if it does not exist. Must be a valid path string.

validators.error_message: base_dir must be a non-empty path string.

fields.name: holdout_percentage
fields.description: Fraction of examples to hold out for the validation/test set. Split is computed at read time via SHA-256 hash of the input field, so changing this value does not require data migration.

validators.error_message: holdout_percentage must be between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive.

fields.name: fine_tune_batch_size
fields.description: Number of training-set examples (not total, not validation) required before signaling batch_ready=True from add_example(). Must be a positive integer.

validators.error_message: fine_tune_batch_size must be a positive integer.

types.description: Configuration for the filesystem-backed TrainingDataStore implementation. Validated strictly at construction time — fails fast on invalid config per project standards.

types.name: AddExampleResult

fields.name: task_type
fields.description: The task type of the example that was just added.

fields.name: example_count
fields.description: Total number of examples stored for this task type (training + validation) after the addition.

validators.error_message: example_count must be at least 1 after a successful add.

fields.name: training_count
fields.description: Number of examples in the training split for this task type after the addition.

fields.name: validation_count
fields.description: Number of examples in the validation split for this task type after the addition.

fields.name: batch_ready
fields.description: True when the training-set count has reached or exceeded fine_tune_batch_size. Signals that a fine-tuning job should be initiated. Will be True on every add once threshold is crossed (not just the first crossing), so callers must track whether they have already acted on this signal.

types.description: Return value from add_example(), providing updated counts and a batch-ready signal. The batch_ready flag is the explicit signaling mechanism for fine-tuning orchestration — no hidden callbacks or side-channel communication.

types.name: ExampleCount

fields.name: task_type
fields.description: The task type these counts apply to.

fields.name: total
fields.description: Total number of examples stored for this task type.

fields.name: training
fields.description: Number of examples in the training split.

fields.name: validation
fields.description: Number of examples in the validation split.

types.description: Summary of example counts for a specific task type, broken down by split.

types.name: TrainingExampleList

functions.name: add_example
functions.description: Appends a single training example to the JSONL file for its task type. The example is serialized as one JSON line and appended to {base_dir}/{task_type}.jsonl. Updates the _counts.json metadata file atomically. Returns an AddExampleResult indicating updated counts and whether the fine-tune batch size threshold has been reached for the training split. The example is appended without rewriting existing data. The deterministic split assignment (training vs. validation) is computed via SHA-256 hash of the input field.

inputs.name: example
inputs.description: The training example to persist. Must pass all field validations (non-empty input/output, valid task_type format, ISO 8601 timestamp).

error_cases.name: validation_error
error_cases.condition: The TrainingExample fails Pydantic field validation (empty input, empty output, invalid task_type format, invalid timestamp format).

error_data.detail: Pydantic validation error message describing which field(s) failed.

error_cases.name: io_error_write
error_cases.condition: The filesystem write to the JSONL file fails (disk full, permission denied, path too long, etc.).

error_data.path: The JSONL file path that could not be written.

error_cases.name: io_error_counts
error_cases.condition: The _counts.json metadata file cannot be read or written during count update.

error_cases.name: serialization_error
error_cases.condition: The example metadata dict contains values that are not JSON-serializable.

preconditions: TrainingDataStoreConfig has been validated and the store has been initialized.
example.task_type matches the pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-]+$ and is 1-128 characters.
example.timestamp is a valid ISO 8601 datetime string.
postconditions: The example has been appended as exactly one new JSON line at the end of {base_dir}/{task_type}.jsonl.
The JSONL file for the task type exists on disk.
The _counts.json file has been updated to reflect the new total count for the task type.
The returned AddExampleResult.example_count equals the previous total count + 1.
The returned AddExampleResult.training_count + AddExampleResult.validation_count == AddExampleResult.example_count.
AddExampleResult.batch_ready is True if and only if training_count >= fine_tune_batch_size.
No existing lines in the JSONL file have been modified or rewritten.
base_dir directory has been auto-created if it did not exist.

structured_side_effects.description: Appends one JSON line to the JSONL file for the given task type.
Updates the count metadata file with the new total for the task type.
Logs the addition event with task_type, example_count, and batch_ready status as structured JSON.

functions.name: iter_training_examples
functions.description: Returns an iterator over all training-split examples for the given task type. Reads from {base_dir}/{task_type}.jsonl and yields only examples whose SHA-256 hash-based split assignment is 'training' (i.e., hash modulo 10000 >= holdout_percentage * 10000). Corrupt JSONL lines are skipped with a logged warning. The split is computed at read time, so changing holdout_percentage in config will change which examples appear in training vs. validation without data migration.

inputs.name: task_type
inputs.description: The task type identifier to iterate training examples for. Must match the format ^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-]+$.

validators.error_message: task_type must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores.

error_cases.condition: The task_type string does not match the required format.

error_cases.name: io_error_read

preconditions: TrainingDataStoreConfig has been validated and the store has been initialized.
postconditions: All returned examples have split assignment 'training' based on SHA-256 hash of example.input.

functions.name: get_example_count
functions.description: Returns the total, training, and validation example counts for a specific task type. Uses the cached _counts.json for the total count and computes the training/validation split counts. If the task type has no stored examples, returns an ExampleCount with all counts at zero.

validators.error_message: task_type must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores.

ExampleCount.task_type == the input task_type.

functions.name: initialize
functions.description: Initializes the Training Data Store with the given configuration. Creates the base_dir directory (including parents) if it does not exist. Loads or reconciles _counts.json against actual JSONL files on disk. Must be called before any other method. Fails fast on invalid configuration per project standards.

invariants: For any task_type, the set of training examples and validation examples are disjoint and their union equals all valid examples in the JSONL file.

The split assignment for an example is deterministic and depends solely on SHA-256(example.input.encode('utf-8')): last 4 bytes as unsigned int, modulo 10000, compared against holdout_percentage * 10000. Values < threshold are validation; values >= threshold are training.
ExampleCount.total == ExampleCount.training + ExampleCount.validation for every task_type at all times.
_counts.json total for a task_type always equals the number of valid (non-corrupt) JSONL lines in {base_dir}/{task_type}.jsonl after reconciliation.
JSONL files are append-only: existing lines are never modified, reordered, or deleted by store operations.
Each line in a JSONL file is a complete, independent JSON object representing one TrainingExample.
No global mutable state: all state is scoped to the store instance and its filesystem backing.
All configuration is validated at initialization time; runtime operations never silently default on missing or invalid config.
AddExampleResult.batch_ready is True if and only if training_count >= config.fine_tune_batch_size.
The same input string always maps to the same split (training or validation) for a given holdout_percentage, regardless of when the example was added or what other examples exist.
Task types returned by get_task_types() are always sorted alphabetically and contain no duplicates.
Corrupt JSONL lines are never yielded by iterators; they are skipped with structured log warnings including line number and parse error detail.
